chunks: It is not for you to guide them, but God guides whom He will. And whatever you spend of good, it is for yourselves, and you do not spend except seeking the countenance of God. And whatever you spend of good, it will be paid back to you in full, and you will not be wronged.

key_terms.يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ: It will be paid back to you in full

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of spending in charity for oneself in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse clarifies the distinction between the Prophet's role as a messenger and God's absolute authority over guidance, often linked to the concept of *Tawfiq*. It further establishes that charitable spending (*Infaq*) is primarily for the purification of the giver's soul, promising complete recompense (*Wafā'*) without any diminution of reward, a principle emphasized by scholars like Al-Tabarsi and Al-Majlisi.
